editorial.headline: Natural-Medicine Raw Materials, Open Nationally and Usable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A precise KBLI for processing extracts, simplisia, galenic preparations, additives, and other inputs used in natural-medicine production for humans.
editorial.body:
This activity sits upstream in the natural-medicine chain. The record describes an industry for processing many kinds of extracts and simplisia, galenic preparations, additives, and other materials used in making natural medicines for humans. Some of those materials may have active properties and some may not; some may be transformed in processing and some may remain substantially unchanged. The important point is functional: these are inputs used in the processing of natural-medicine products, even where not every original ingredient remains visible in the bulk product.

That makes the code useful for founders whose business is not the retail face of wellness, nor the branding of finished consumer products, but the industrial preparation of the materials behind them. It is a production-side classification: a way to place extraction, preparation, and ingredient handling inside the formal KBLI map without overstating the activity as finished-medicine manufacturing. A company using this code should be able to describe its work in the language of the record: processing extracts, simplisia, galenic preparations, additives, or other materials for use in natural-medicine production for humans.

The scale picture is broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so it can describe a small operation as well as a larger industrial setup, provided the actual business remains within this scope. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the national record treats this activity as open to foreign investment up to full foreign ownership. That is a strong national signal, and it should not be diluted into a vague caveat.

The Bali picture is also clear, and in this case it does not overturn the national openness. The record marks Bali as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason: OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, but this record is not marked as blocked. The honest reading is therefore simple: nationally this activity is foreign-open, and for Bali the record does not mark it as blocked by the moratorium.
